views.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: single photorealistic interior design mockup, portrait, no collage.
Input image 1 is the actual entrance EDIT TARGET. Use its exact room, narrow proportions, camera position and architecture. Decor changes only. The user wants a much more characterful traditional English / Arts and Crafts entrance, layered and collected, while retaining actual paint and furniture.
LOCK: exact front door and its tulip stained glass, curved green lower bands, fanlight and exterior lantern, narrow right stained-glass sidelight, brass door hardware, wall colours, white panelling, cornice, three ribbed glass pendants, black steel glazed lounge door at left, actual grey/black/ivory STAR MOSAIC tiles in original scale. Keep the existing dark curved demi-lune console with its drawer and turned legs and hammered dark rectangular mirror at right. Preserve foreground white newel. Do not replace mirror, enlarge table, widen room or change architectural openings. Exact original floor pattern, NOT diamond tiles.
DECOR:
- Remove existing white coat pole, towel, clutter, clock, jacket on newel.
- In right sidelight nook place a compact traditional dark walnut turned-wood hall coat stand, restrained 3 small aged brass acorn-ended hooks, one olive jacket and dark dog lead. Around 170 cm tall, compact weighted round base 32-35 cm. Slim and elegant, not huge spreading bentwood or modern angular coat tree; retain sidelight visibility.
- Keep actual rectangular wicker lidded dog hamper, propose it beneath existing console between legs; no artificial resizing of basket/table.
- Transform the console styling noticeably: a SMALL traditional aged-brass barley-twist lamp at door end, approx 38-40 cm high with a 20-22 cm wide gently pleated olive/tobacco green fabric shade with cream lining and a fine rust trim, softly illuminated; compact aspidistra broad deep green foliage at opposite end in a small antique moss-green glazed ceramic jardiniere, 16-18cm diameter, restrained relief detail; at centre two slim old clothbound books in brown and ochre with unreadable spines, a tiny blue-and-white porcelain key saucer sitting on them; a very small oval antique brass picture frame leaning at back below mirror, with a tiny sepia landscape illustration (not a person). Compose with realistic space and scale, do not fill entire table with clutter. Mirror remains functional. Books, porcelain and vintage frame add personal collected character, not hotel staging.
- Keep a simple natural coir doormat with a thin cocoa border at front door, door-width, most geometric tiled entrance left exposed. Brown Persian runner belongs down the hall BEHIND camera, do not invent Persian carpet in entrance square.
- Optional small glimpse of traditional landscape art reflected naturally in mirror only if physically valid; do not paint over glass or add floating frames.
Light: balanced natural daylight retaining pale grey wall paint, warm local lamp pool and existing pendant glow, realistic shadows, timber patina, woven shade, glazed ceramic. Warm, inviting, authentic existing home, photograph not illustration or glossy CGI.
No stair carpet (any visible stairs must be bare oak), no new cabinetry, bench, wall repaint, extra floor furniture, wall sconces or structural changes. No text, captions, labels, watermarks. Single photographic view.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: single photorealistic interior design study, tall portrait, no collage.
Input image 1 is the actual hallway EDIT TARGET. Show this same actual hallway looking past oak stairs to kitchen and garden. User specifically rejects stair carpets and modern botanical pictures. They want a faded brown Persian-style hall runner and THREE traditional landscape paintings hung diagonally on the PLAIN WALL ABOVE THE STAIR PANELLING, not inside the panels.
PRESERVE EXACT HOUSE: oak stair treads AND oak risers FULLY EXPOSED with original grain, white turned newel and balusters, dark handrail; ALL existing wall panelling mouldings and sloping upper trim in their original positions and height; same pale grey wall and white paint, flush tall cupboards with same seams, black steel glazed lounge door right, rear door and transom, kitchen and garden view, ceiling cornice/downlights/detector. Preserve exact intricate black/grey/ivory STAR MOSAIC floor tiles wherever exposed, at original scale. No modified floor or stair geometry, no invented joinery.
FRAMING: the supplied photo crops much of the blank upper stair wall at the top/left. EXTEND THE VIEW UPWARDS AND TO THE LEFT as needed to reveal more of that upper wall and show the diagonal paintings. Keep original photographed architectural geometry and narrow hallway width. This is a slight upward/wider framing extension, not lowering/removing/rebuilding the panelling to make room for art. Original top sloping panelling trim stays below the paintings. It is fine for nearest painting to be partially cropped if necessary. No fake window or other new architecture. Maintain a believable camera viewpoint.
CHANGES:
1. Remove jacket from newel, cap from steps and foreground temporary clutter. Leave oak stairs completely bare from bottom to top. ABSOLUTELY NO STAIR RUNNER, carpet, stair rods or fabric tread pads. All oak risers also bare.
2. On tiled hall walkway only, a beautiful aged traditional Persian-style wool runner, about 60cm wide, realistically scaled length leaving bare tiles before rear door and at entrance. Main colours tobacco brown, walnut, camel and muted warm taupe, with very restrained faded rust, ivory and tiny charcoal/olive details. Rich intricate traditional floral/herati drawing and a quiet sequence of small medallions, softly worn antique surface, low contrast and matte, not bright orange, red or beige solid strip. A defined traditional brown multi-band border. Fine flat low pile, no long fringe, no fake shiny rug. Continuous original tile margins 12-17cm each side. Rug lies flat, no doors obstructed. Let wool, warm wood and original tiled floor form a traditional collected composition.
3. Three different TRADITIONAL representational English pastoral LANDSCAPE PAINTINGS, small old oil-painting character, in slim-to-medium dark aged gilt frames with patinated detailing, no large white modern mounts. Scenes: a wooded river with bridge, a misty meadow with trees, a small rural cottage and lane. Soft brown, ochre, muted moss and ivory; painterly fine detail, NOT abstract, geometric, modern botanical poster or graphic line art. Hang them horizontally level, with centres rising diagonally parallel to stair. Entire frames are ON THE PLAIN WALL ABOVE THE UPPERMOST SLOPING PANELLING TRIM, with 10-15cm air above moulding. Do NOT put paintings inside rectangular panelling or overlap mouldings. Painting overall sizes around 30x40 to 35x45cm, fitting available upper wall; preserve trim geometry even if a painting must crop at edge. Three complementary but non-identical vintage gilt frames make a collected gallery.
4. Keep circulation uncluttered, cupboards and doors fully usable. No new hall floor furniture, benches, console in this angle or plants on steps.
Soft real daylight from garden, gently balanced photographic exposure, exact unchanged wall paint. Warm natural oak and antique brown rug, quietly rich period atmosphere. Photorealistic existing home, no cinematic filters or illustration. No people, text, captions, arrows or watermark.
views.framing: Generated view extends the upper/left stair wall beyond source coverage to illustrate art above the panelling; this extension and its proportions are inferred, not a survey.

notes: Each image generated in one call. The earlier generated designs were not used as edit targets to limit cumulative drift. Exact prompts retained; generation is not deterministic. Original sources and earlier iteration files left unchanged. Final outputs copied without post-processing.
